assignments.title: VR Activity: Standing on the Causeway
assignments.html:
VR ACTIVITY
Standing on the Causeway
Solo · one in-headset session
16 points · file upload or text entry
❦ ❧ ❦
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you write. Then take part in the session and submit your work in this assignment.

WHAT YOU'RE DOING

In the lessons you read how Moctezuma met Cortés on a causeway and let him into Tenochtitlan. In your VR headset you will stand in a reconstructed city of the ancient Americas and judge the space for yourself. Your task is to decide what the layout of the city made easy for the Mexica and what it made dangerous.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED
▶
Your VR headset, charged and ready
▶
Your course page for this week, which lists the session link and the place to enter
▶
A notebook or open document for quick notes while you are in the session
▶
About 45 minutes in one sitting
HOW TO JOIN
Where to go: Open your immersive session from the link on your course page, then enter the location named there.
Solo or group: Solo. You do not need a partner.
If something fails: Write down what happened and use the help contact on your course page. Do not skip the activity.
WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER
1
Review first. Skim this module’s lessons again, paying attention to the causeways, the canals, and the entry of Cortés.
2
Enter and look around. Spend at least ten minutes moving slowly through the space. Take in the size of the city, the water around it, and the narrow ways in and out.
3
Stop at three places. Choose three spots that matter most for how the city could be defended or entered. At each one, use your headset's capture tool to take a picture, and jot a note about what you see.
4
Test an idea. Stand where a column of soldiers would have to walk in single file. Ask yourself what the space would have allowed a defender to do, and what it would have allowed an invader to do.
5
Write your response. After you leave the session, write one paragraph of about 150 to 200 words that answers this question: What does the layout of the city suggest about the choice Moctezuma made, and about how easily it could have gone another way?
WHAT TO SUBMIT

Submit your three captured images and your paragraph in the Canvas assignment. Use the images as evidence in your writing, and name which picture you are referring to.

Estimated time: 45 minutes

SUCCESS CRITERIA
☐
I spent at least ten minutes moving through the space.
☐
I captured three images that show different parts of the space.
☐
My paragraph uses at least two of my images as evidence.
☐
My paragraph connects what I saw to what I read in this module’s lessons.
☐
I wrote in complete sentences and kept to about 150 to 200 words.
FACILITATOR NOTE

Teacher-facing. Before releasing this activity, add the session link and the specific location to the course page, and confirm that students have a way to capture images in their headsets. The instructions above are platform-neutral on purpose. Grade with the course rubric for VR activities: three images as evidence, a paragraph that cites them, and reasoning tied to the lesson.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: Spain's Silver Empire
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
Spain's Silver Empire
2 questions · survey · one attempt
❦ ❧ ❦
Essential question for this week
How could a few hundred Spaniards bring down two great empires, and what did the conquest do for Spain?
Instructions

Welcome to Spain's Silver Empire. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

Cortés and the Fall of the Aztec Empire

  • Describe the Mexica empire of 1519 and how it held its subjects.
  • Explain how Cortés, his translators, and his native allies brought down Tenochtitlan.
  • Weigh the roles of disease, allies, weapons, and chance in the Spanish victory.

Pizarro, the Inca, and the Silver of Potosí

  • Explain how Pizarro captured the Inca emperor and why the Inca state was vulnerable in 1532.
  • Describe how Potosí silver was mined and how forced labor supplied it.
  • Evaluate whether silver made Spain strong.

discussions.title: Discussion: Why Did Two Empires Fall to a Few Hundred Spaniards?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Why Did Two Empires Fall to a Few Hundred Spaniards?
Spain's Silver Empire
10 points · threaded discussion
❦ ❧ ❦
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week you read how about five hundred Spaniards brought down the Mexica empire and how 168 men captured the Inca emperor. The lessons give several reasons, and they do not all carry the same weight.

Choose the one reason that you think did the most to explain why these empires fell. It might be disease, native allies, weapons, the way each empire was ruled, or chance. State your choice, then defend it with at least two specific details from the lessons. Finish by naming the strongest argument against your choice, and say why you still hold it.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate who chose a different reason from yours. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Makes a clear choice, supports it with at least two specific details from the lessons, and names a fair argument against it. Makes a choice but gives only one detail, or stays general, or leaves out the counterargument. No post, or no clear choice.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
